title: 2009 HMMT February General Round 2 Problem 5
statement: Suppose \(a, b\) and \(c\) are integers such that the greatest common divisor of \(x^{2}+a x+b\) and \(x^{2}+b x+c\) is \(x+1\) (in the set of polynomials in \(x\) with integer coefficients), and the least common multiple of \(x^{2}+a x+b\) and \(x^{2}+b x+c\) is \(x^{3}-4 x^{2}+x+6\). Find \(a+b+c\).

solutions.text:
Since \(x+1\) divides \(x^{2}+a x+b\) and the constant term is \(b\), we have \(x^{2}+a x+b=(x+1)(x+b)\), and similarly \(x^{2}+b x+c=(x+1)(x+c)\). Therefore, \(a=b+1=c+2\). Furthermore, the least common
multiple of the two polynomials is \((x+1)(x+b)(x+b-1)=x^{3}-4 x^{2}+x+6\), so \(b=-2\). Thus \(a=-1\) and \(c=-3\), and \(a+b+c=-6\).
